prompt: How do I find an email with advanced search in Outlook?
completion:
Below is a quick‑start guide for using **Advanced Search** in Microsoft Outlook. I’ve split it into two sections: 1. **Desktop App (Office 365 / Outlook 2016‑2021)** 2. **Outlook Web App (OWA / Outlook.com)** Feel free to copy‑paste any of the query snippets into the search box or the Advanced Find dialog; they’ll work right away. --- ## 1. Desktop Outlook (Windows & macOS) | Step | What you see | Action | |------|--------------|--------| | **1** | **Click the Search box** (above your message list) | Outlook automatically shows the **Search** tab in the ribbon. | | **2** | **Search tab** appears. | You’ll see groups: *Scope*, *Refine*, *Results*, *Tools*. | | **3** | **Advanced Find** | Two ways: | | | • **Press** `Ctrl + Shift + F` (Windows) or `⌘ + Shift + F` (Mac).
• Or click **Search > Search Tools > Advanced Find…** | Opens the “Advanced Find” dialog. | | **4** | In the **Advanced Find** dialog, you’ll see tabs: **Messages**, **Look for**, **Advanced**, **More choices**, **Search**. | Use these tabs to set conditions. | | **5** | **Messages tab** (default) | Choose the folder(s) to search – e.g. *Inbox*, *All Mail*, or a specific sub‑folder. | | **6** | **Advanced tab** | Here you can add multiple search criteria. Click **Field**, choose the property (From, To, Subject, Body, Has Attachments, etc.), then set the condition (contains, equals, etc.). | | **7** | **Add conditions** | You can combine up to 30 conditions with **AND** / **OR**. Example:
• **From** contains `alice@example.com` **AND**
• **Subject** contains `Quarterly Report` **AND**
• **Has Attachments** is `Yes`. | | **8** | **Click “Find Now”** | Outlook will list all matching messages. | | **9** | **Save a Search Folder** (optional) | In the **Search** tab, click **Search Tools > Save Search**. This creates a search folder that updates automatically. | ### Quick‑look syntax (same in both Desktop & Web) If you’re comfortable typing directly in the Search box, Outlook supports a concise query language: | Syntax | Example | Meaning | |--------|---------|---------| | `from:alice@example.com` | `from:alice@example.com` | Messages sent by Alice | | `to:bob@example.com` | `to:bob@example.com` | Messages sent to Bob | | `subject:"Quarterly Report"` | `subject:"Quarterly Report"` | Subject contains the phrase | | `hasattachment:true` | `hasattachment:true` | Only messages that have attachments | | `size:>5MB` | `size:>5MB` | Attachments larger than 5 MB | | `received:2024-01-01..2024-01-31` | `received:2024-01-01..2024-01-31` | Received in January 2024 | | `category:"Follow Up"` | `category:"Follow Up"` | Messages tagged with the “Follow Up” category | | `notfrom:spam@example.com` | `notfrom:spam@example.com` | Exclude messages from spam@example.com | | `from:alice@example.com AND subject:"Quarterly Report"` | `from:alice@example.com AND subject:"Quarterly Report"` | Both conditions must be true | > **Tip:** You can combine any of the above with **AND**, **OR**, and parentheses for complex queries. --- ## 2. Outlook Web App (OWA) / Outlook.com | Step | What you see | Action | |------|--------------|--------| | **1** | **Search bar** at the top of the page | Click it or press `Ctrl + E` (Windows) / `⌘ + E` (Mac). | | **2** | **Filter button** (funnel icon) | Click to open the drop‑down filter panel. | | **3** | **Choose filter criteria** | You can filter by **From**, **To**, **Subject**, **Has attachment**, **Size**, **Date received**, **Categories**, etc. | | **4** | **Type additional keywords** | After filtering, you can also type plain text to match anywhere in the email. | | **5** | **Advanced query** | In the search bar, type the same query syntax shown above (`from:`, `subject:`, etc.). | | **6** | **Save a Search** | OWA doesn’t have a built‑in “Save Search” like desktop, but you can create a **Saved Search** via the *View* options if you’re in the *Outlook.com* web interface, or use a third‑party add‑in. | ### Example OWA Search ``` from:alice@example.com AND subject:"Quarterly Report" AND hasattachment:true ``` After typing this, press **Enter**. The results will automatically reflect the criteria. --- ## Common “Gotchas” & Tips | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Search not finding emails in sub‑folders** | In Advanced Find, set **Scope** to *All folders* or choose the parent folder. In OWA, ensure you’re searching “All mail” or the specific folder. | | **Attachments not being found** | Use `hasattachment:true` (or `hasattachment:false`) – the boolean is required. | | **Date ranges** | OWA uses `received:yyyy-mm-dd..yyyy-mm-dd`. Desktop supports the same. | | **Case‑sensitive?** | Outlook’s search is case‑insensitive. | | **Search language** | If your account uses a language other than English, some field names may be localized. The query syntax, however, stays in English. | | **Performance** | Searching a huge mailbox can take a while. Narrow the scope or use filters to speed things up. | | **Search folders** | Once you’ve created a search folder (desktop), you can double‑click it anytime to refresh the results. | --- ### Quick‑start cheat sheet | Task | Desktop (Keyboard) | OWA (Keyboard) | |------|--------------------|----------------| | Open Advanced Find | `Ctrl + Shift + F` | `Ctrl + E` → **Filter** → *Advanced* | | Search “from Alice” | `from:alice@example.com` | `from:alice@example.com` | | Search “subject contains QBR” | `subject:"QBR"` | `subject:"QBR"` | | Search with attachments | `hasattachment:true` | `hasattachment:true` | | Search a date range | `received:2024-01-01..2024-01-31` | Same | Use these snippets to zero‑in on the exact message you need. Once you get comfortable, you’ll be able to locate any email in seconds—no matter how many messages you have!
